name: Gin Rummy
description: Gin Rummy is a two-player knock-rummy game where players draw and discard to build sets and runs, then end a hand by knocking with low deadwood or going gin with no deadwood.

content.text: Gin Rummy is a two-player knock-rummy game where players draw and discard to build sets and runs, then end a hand by knocking with low deadwood or going gin with no deadwood.
Gin Rummy was created by New York Bridge player Elwood T. Baker around 1911, from the Mexican game Conquian and the American game Rum.

Two players only, head-to-head; no partnerships. Each player receives ten cards per hand. Dealership alternates from round to round; the first dealer is often chosen by drawing cards from the pack (lower card deals), and subsequently the winner of the previous hand deals.
Standard 52-card deck, ace low in runs.
Scorepad for cumulative hand and game bonuses.
Deal 10 cards to each player one at a time. Turn the next card face up as first discard and place the rest face down as stock.

items.text: 25-Point Bonus Tables: Some groups use 25 for gin bonus and/or undercut bonus instead of 20 and 10.
Oklahoma Gin: Initial upcard value sets knock limit and a spade upcard doubles hand score; game target is often 150.
11-Card Non-Dealer Start: Alternative opening deals 11 to non-dealer and 10 to dealer with no upcard, then non-dealer discards first.
